details:
Lunar Site Compare is an interactive web-based tool developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to help identify and compare potential lunar landing sites near the Moon's south pole. It allows users to compare up to three locations and dates, visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth through a 3D lunar globe and horizon view, and explore sunlight and communication availability over a complete lunar day. The tool evaluates six key factors: sunlit time, longest darkness, peak Sun elevation, Earth visibility, longest communication gap, and periods when both sunlight and communication are available.

The project's main benefit is simplifying complex astronomical data into accessible visualizations that support better lunar landing-site decisions. Its intended impact is to help mission planners evaluate locations more efficiently, understand environmental challenges, and identify sites with better conditions for solar power and communication with Earth. The project uses browser-based calculations, low-precision lunar and solar ephemeris models, and optical libration to estimate the positions of celestial bodies. All calculations run directly in the browser. Its creativity lies in bringing multiple astronomical calculations, interactive visualizations, and side-by-side site comparisons into one platform. Our team considered sunlight availability, communication reliability, lunar terrain, changing celestial positions, and the practical limitations of astronomical modelling when developing the solution.
